sections.h2: Who mails the Colquitt County bill?
sections.html:
The Moultrie Tax Commissioner handles mailing and collection. Value comes from the Tax Assessor's Office, and the commissioner controls neither value nor millage.

Visit 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, GA 31768, or write to postal box 99. Counter hours are 8:00am to 4:30pm, Monday through Friday, and you can reach property tax staff at (229) 616-7410. The same office runs motor vehicle registration. Solid waste has its own desk at 101 East Central Avenue, Office 168, (229) 616-7405, and the landfill opens Saturdays from 8:00am to noon, handy when you are cleaning out a house before listing.

  • Assessor's Office: appraisals, assessment notices, exemption approvals.
  • Board of Equalization: hears appeals, with members the grand jury appoints.
  • County commission and school board: separate mill rates, set separately.
  • Tax Commissioner: the bill itself, payment, liens and levies.

This is Southwest Georgia farm country, about 557 square miles, its courthouse and biggest city both in Moultrie. US 319 connects Moultrie to Interstate 75 roughly 24 miles east.

An estimated 47,438 people lived here in 2025, in 19,775 housing units, and 63.7% of homes were owner-occupied. Median owned value is $121,400 and gross rent is $818, so price a listing with that modest market in view.

Real estate and business personal property are generally due December 10, with mailing at least 60 days before. Go by the date your own bill prints, because it can shift.

Bills carry the owner's name, not the lender's. When a mortgage has no escrow, passing the bill to the lender is your job. The office cannot guarantee delivery, and interest, penalty and costs apply either way.

Manufactured and mobile homes have a deadline of their own, and the Tax Commissioner can tell you yours. Before moving a unit into or out of the county, get a relocation permit from the Compliance office in the Courthouse Annex at 229-616-7417.

Past the due date a bill picks up interest monthly and, later, a penalty. Rather than calculating it yourself, request a written payoff. Homesteaded parcels with bills under $500 owe no penalty.

If nothing is paid, a FiFa follows. That tax lien is entered at the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket and can stay on a credit record for at least seven years. The commissioner may also levy against the property and in the end sell it, though levy is meant as a last resort.

Delinquent notices go out only periodically, so the figure on the last one you got may have grown by the time you pay or close.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when the house sells
sections.html:
Ownership on January 1 decides who is on the hook. If you held the house that day, the bill and any lien stay yours even after a June sale. You can move the debt to the buyer by handing the commissioner the closing statement no later than 90 days after the due date.

When your closing prorates the tax, take the settlement statement to the East Central Avenue office. That lets the commissioner record a lien against the new owner if the bill goes unpaid. Any bill that arrives for a house you have already sold belongs with the buyer, so forward it.

Ask the title company how the county gets its money, and obtain a payoff from the commissioner dated near the closing. A recorded lien will not stop a sale. Its payoff comes out of the sale funds at the table. A cash buyer closes the same way, minus a lender to satisfy. Bring the deed, your latest bill and any lien paperwork.

Colquitt offers a standard exemption plus several based on age, military service or income. Each is subtracted from assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40% of fair market value. File your first application with the Tax Assessor's Office, with a copy of your warranty deed if you just bought. It has to be in their hands by April 1.

  • Standard homestead: takes $2,000 off assessed value for county, school and state levies.
  • Elderly school tax (62 or older): up to $10,000 off, if net income is $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general (65 or older): up to $4,000 off, with a $10,000 income test that leaves out Social Security and some retirement income.
  • Disabled veteran or qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption (62 or older): gross household income of $30,000 or less, covering state and county tax but not school tax.

Where a local exemption is larger than the state amount, the local one wins. The assessors can tell you which applies. Farmland has its own paths: assessment at 30% for bona fide agricultural use, and conservation use or timber programs that require a covenant of at least 10 years. Historic property and certain hazardous-site redevelopment parcels may also qualify. Owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until a sale or until the deferral and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

sections.h2: What a seller should do before listing
sections.html:
Call the Tax Commissioner at (229) 616-7410 first and ask what is owed today, including any open FiFa. Because of the January 1 rule, the bill may still carry your name at closing. If the house had a homestead exemption, plan to tell the Tax Assessor's Office after the sale so it comes off your account, and expect the buyer to apply on their own.

Give the title company the deed and the bill. If the closing prorates the tax, keep the settlement statement safe: the commissioner needs it within 90 days after the due date for the buyer to be billed. A seller with a mobile home on the lot should also check the relocation permit rule before anyone moves the unit.

Write the appeal and file it within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The choices are the equalization board or an arbitrator, and either result can go on to Superior Court.

Through April 1 each spring you may also file a return giving your own opinion of the property's January 1 value. Say nothing and you are treated as returning last year's value and exemptions. For a mobile home, the sequence is 45 days to appeal to the assessors, then 21 days from their notice to go to the equalization board.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Colquitt County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Tax Commissioner's office at 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, any weekday between 8:00am and 4:30pm. A convenience fee from the card company applies to card payments.

faqs.q: What date is Colquitt County property tax normally due?
faqs.a: Usually December 10 for real estate and business personal property. The date printed on your bill is the one to follow, since it can change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Colquitt County house with a recorded tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid off from the sale funds at closing. Get a current figure from the commissioner and give it to the title company.

faqs.q: Which Colquitt County office takes homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's Office takes them. It must receive yours by April 1, and a later filing counts toward the next tax year.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Colquitt County assessment?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the date on the notice. Choose the equalization board or an arbitrator, and know that Superior Court is open afterward.
